name: Respiratory variants & flu
value: US flu admissions 9,584 (to 7 Nov); severity low
summary: US flu admissions hit 9,584 in the week to 7 Nov, over seven times a year earlier; CDC still rates severity low
state: CDC reported 9,584 flu hospital admissions in the week to 7 Nov, with seven states at high or very high activity and H1N1 making up nearly all subtyped flu A; it rates in-season severity low for all ages and estimates at least 36,000 hospitalisations and five child deaths so far (CDC). Admissions are running more than seven times last year's level (Becker's Hospital Review). Searches on 21 Nov found no new WHO variant designation and no health systems reported as strained, so an unusually early US season keeps Watch.
for_you: Flu is circulating early in the US. In the UK, the NHS offers free flu vaccination to eligible groups; follow NHS and UKHSA advice if you are in one of them.
rubric_hit: Watch: unusually early US flu season (admissions 7x prior year); no variant of concern or strained health systems

sources.title: CDC — Weekly US Influenza Surveillance Report, week 44, ending November 7, 2026
Becker's Hospital Review — Flu admissions running more than 7x higher than last year

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
